newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won closes lower despite BOK intervention.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won closes lower despite BOK intervention.

text.p: The won fell to an 84-month low against the U.S. dollar on Monday on importer deals and expectations that the won would stay weak, dealers said.
But the won recouped part of its earlier fall by the close after repeated dollar sales by the central bank, brokers said.
The won closed at 866.90, after hitting 867.80, the lowest level seen since March 1990. It touched a high of 864.40.
"The dollar was seen undergoing a technical correction towards the close. But it's too early to say a real correction has started," said a domestic bank dealer.
Another local dealer said many banks were expected to take a wait-and-see attitude until the Lunar New Year holidays, from February 7-9.
The won has been pressured by a snowballing trade deficit and the dollar's strength against the Japanese yen on world markets.
Last week South Korea announced a record monthly trade deficit of $3.48 billion for January.
Dealers expected the won's base mid-rate to be pegged at 866.80 on Tuesday, compared with Monday's 864.50.
